entities.name: Marcus Metilius Aquillius Regulus
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Marcus Metilius Aquillius Regulus was a Roman senator of the second century AD, serving as consul ordinarius in 157 with colleague Marcus Vettulenus Civica Barbarus.

As a member of the patrician order, Regulus was part of the Roman elite, influencing the governance of the empire. His appointment as consul marked a significant event in the history of Rome, reflecting the power dynamics between the patrician class and the Roman people.

Regulus' tenure as consul had a lasting impact on Roman politics, shaping the course of the empire's future.

Despite the significance of his role, Regulus' life remains shrouded in mystery, with limited information available about his personal life or achievements prior to his consulship.

The legacy of Marcus Metilius Aquillius Regulus continues to be felt in the annals of Roman history, a testament to the enduring influence of the Roman senatorial class.

This enigmatic figure remains a fascinating subject of study for historians and scholars seeking to understand the intricacies of Roman politics and society.
